messages:
support-bot: ALERT — Dedicated pool `sparkline-prod` hitting token/s burst SLO. Several clients receiving 429 admission_control. Link: https://internal.redwood/status/alerts/2187654321 :warning:
alex: ack, I'm on it. Which customer reported this?
maria: acme-pay reported repeated 429s starting 06:42 UTC, spike aligns with marketing campaign. They show 3k TPS sustained for ~90s then 429s.
kevin: looking at runtime logs now — I see admission controller dropping after burst_credits=0 for pool sparkline-prod, plus high kernel queue latency on node gpu-07.
sam: repro steps from Acme's side: `curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx","input":"x"}'` in a tight loop at 3k TPS produces 429 within ~60s. They attached a small client script.
maria: posting relevant snippet of admission log: ```TIME=2026-02-15T06:42:13Z pool=sparkline-prod admit=reject reason=burst_credits_exhausted account=acme-pay tps=3120 headroom_ms=45```
kevin: also seeing KV-cache eviction warnings and slower kv-attach times, likely due to memory pressure on gpu-07. Noisy neighbor suspected (tenant id=zephyr-spend had abnormal seq_len and long-lived sessions).
alex: can we confirm autoscaler didn't spin up extra replicas?
ops-bot: Autoscaler event: scale_up triggered but prewarm=false, new nodes pending provisioning 2m 14s. Autoscale lag > configured 60s.
kevin: autoscaler lag is due to a cloud image pull rate + node init hook timeout. That explains why admission fell back instead of smoothing.
sam: immediate mitigation options?
kevin: short-term: 1) bump pool burst_credits for acme-pay by +6000 for 10m, 2) route acme-pay to auxiliary pool `sparkline-burst` (hot spare), or 3) temporarily throttle noisy tenant (zephyr-spend) to reduce contention.
iris: billing note — acme-pay has burst credits bucket 0 right now. If we bump, they'll consume from transient credits and we'll reconcile. Need billing signoff for >$X.
alex: can we route them to `sparkline-burst` without client changes?
kevin: yes, create a route rule for account=acme-pay -> pool=sparkline-burst. I can push the rule; it's a config change: ```PATCH /v1/admin/routes {"match":{"account":"acme-pay"},"route_to":"sparkline-burst"}```
maria: agree this is least customer-impact. If we route them, we still need to debug root cause on gpu-07.
sam: please do route and bump burst credits as fallback. I'll notify Acme support.
kevin: routing rule applied. Confirmed 06:45:12 UTC: traffic for acme-pay draining to sparkline-burst.
ops-bot: Pool `sparkline-burst` admission OK, latency stable at p95=120ms.
maria: Acme confirms reduced 429s. They're still seeing higher latency for long sequences.
kevin: opened infra ticket INF-8421 to investigate GPU contention and image pull delays. Assigned to eng-infra. Suggested checks: node-level dmesg, CUDA mig usage, cgroup throttling, and recent image changes.
alex: action items: 1) kevin — follow infra ticket and patch admission fallback to add hysteresis (ETA 48h), 2) eng-infra — investigate gpu-07 contention (ETA 24h), 3) ops — consider enabling pool prewarm by default for high-SLO accounts, 4) support (sam) — confirm Acme SLA impact and billing offset.
kevin: temp workaround scripts I used: ```# route change
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://internal.api/v1/admin/routes -d '{"match":{"account":"acme-pay"},"route_to":"sparkline-burst"}'
# bump credits
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $BILLING" https://internal.api/v1/admin/burst_credit -d '{"account":"acme-pay","credits":6000,"ttl":"10m"}'
```
irs: :thinking: small typo — billing user is `iris`, not `irs`.
iris: billing approves temporary +6000 transient credits. I'll post invoice note.
sam: Acme co. confirms 429s dropped to <1% after routing. Will monitor for 2h then close.
kevin: leaving trace of evidence for postmortem: admission reject times, autoscale events, kernel queue histograms, noisy-tenant sessions. Recommend adding a test to loadrunner to simulate long-tailed sequence length tenants.
alex: thanks all. Reopen if 429s reappear.
ops-bot: Incident resolved status: mitigated at 2026-02-15T06:47:30Z by route change. Monitoring channel will auto-close in 2h unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:
